title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered '-182- IX' with a handwritten correction. It belongs to the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), from the part treating the transcendental (complex-analytic) variant. It does not belong to the 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. The previous page in the folder is a handwritten computation of v_p(p^n/n!), which is unrelated. The page was most likely misfiled, or its paper reused.

Setting:
- S is a complex analytic space and s a point of S.
- A is an analytic group over S whose fibres are extensions of abelian varieties by tori.
- 13.2 introduced the formal completion of A along the fibre A_s, via the infinitesimal neighbourhoods S_n of s and A_n = A x_S S_n.

Section 13.5 ('relatively algebraic case') assumes the following.
1. A comes from a relative scheme in groups over S, in Hakim's sense (ref. [10], relative schemes over a ringed space/topos). This group scheme is smooth and separated, and its fibres are extensions of abelian schemes by tori.
2. The abuse of notation (writing A for both the relative scheme and its analytification) is justified because analytification G -> G^an is fully faithful on this category. The text says this follows from relative GAGA, but does not prove it ('il serait facile à établir').
3. Let O be the analytic local ring of S at s. Near s, the relative scheme is determined by the ordinary scheme A_O over Spec(O).
4. The formal completion of A_O along its closed fibre (which is A_s) coincides with the formal completion of the analytic group A along A_s.
5. Suppose Â, viewed as a formal group scheme over Ô, is algebraizable (ref. 7.2.1). This holds e.g. if S is normal at s and A is quasi-projective (ref. 7.1.5), via the Grothendieck existence theorem. One then gets a group scheme A^♮ over Spec(Ô), an extension of an abelian scheme B_Ô by a torus.
6. For simplicity, B_Ô is assumed projective over Ô. This is automatic when O is normal: then Ô is normal because analytic local rings are excellent, and abelian schemes over normal local bases are projective.

The page ends at 'On va alors prouver :'. The statement to be proved is on the next page, which is not transcribed. It presumably compares the analytic and formal/algebraic Néron-model and monodromy data.
errors: Full faithfulness of G -> G^an is asserted with only a reference to relative GAGA; no proof is given.
The step 'O normal implies Ô normal' tacitly uses the excellence of analytic local rings.
The page has been archived in the wrong context: it is a typescript page of SGA 7 Exp. IX inside cote 136 (divided-power de Rham complex, 1976).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript of already-published SGA 7 material. The only point of interest is the misfiling.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed, not handwritten. Its header '- 182 -  IX' indicates page 182 of Exposé IX of SGA 7.
The superscript on A_Ô, transcribed as ♮, is a handwritten insertion and may be a different decoration symbol.
'(isomorphe à A_s = A_o)': the subscript is o (closed point of Spec O), as transcribed.
